tldr: Finite correlated cluster randomization under raw Horvitz--Thompson analysis admits certified arbitrary-accuracy synthesis over the full Candogan--Chen--Niazadeh common-marginal class. Downward rounding and a discarded-square budget create a small set of weight types. An exact count game retains dependence across types and recovers actual binary assignments at every public rational common marginal \(\pi\in(0,1/2]\), for arbitrary positive rational box endpoints. The headline theorem supplies a quasi-polynomial algorithm, a relative optimal-risk interval, and a compressed sampler; fairness is the sharper-support, software, and \(7/3\)-comparator specialization. Known-index oracle two-block optimality concerns a different quadratic objective; an explicit bounded-outcome family separates its single-pair construction from the robust optimum. The open question is whether the full-class synthesis guarantee admits polynomial time for each fixed tolerance. The benchmark is conditional on retaining raw HT.
gap: The inspected finite robust-game literature provides exponential exact optimization and efficient constant-factor or asymptotic designs, leaving certified finite arbitrary-accuracy synthesis without a stated complexity bound. Known-index oracle optimizers do not supply this robust certificate.
fill: A type-count quotient and a risk-relative rounding certificate produce an executable approximation scheme; a pricing-and-separation question isolates its unresolved polynomial-time frontier. A finite two-block separation distinguishes the objective from oracle design.
